findings.text: The clarification card prints the whole unclear sentence a second time, in bold, as its question (ux/Understand/fixtures.js:22 `ask: \`"${s}" — take that literally…\``). On a phone that is four more lines of text right under the same sentence (proof/understand-400-clarified.png). The card already sits directly under the sentence, so the ask can be just "Take that literally, or as a rough idea to refine together?"

Once an option is picked, the card's header says "Decided by owner" (proof/understand-400-clarified.png). That text comes from Decision and is false in a demo that any visitor can click. ClarifyCard (ux/Understand/Understand.js:692) should hide it or change it, for example to "Your choice".

Everything the brief asked for is there: both modules, the exported `marks()` and `rename_options()`, the fixtures fallback with its one-line notice, the in-memory logs, the children line, and the 400px and 1920px proof shots with the dropdown open and a choice made (proof/). Nothing in the diff looks broken, and `.ac("")` at Rename.js:340 is safe because View.ac skips empty strings.

In the Rename dropdown, "Keep current" is the option already selected, so choosing it never fires `change` (ux/Rename/Rename.js:376–379). The dropdown stays open and Cancel is the only way out, which contradicts doc/decisions.md "Keep current is a real option". A disabled "Pick a name…" placeholder as the first option would fix it.

In the 1920 and 3440 shots, the three Rename titles look like plain h3 headings (127-0-0-1-51851-framework-ux-Rename/sheet.png). Nothing shows they can be tapped until one is selected. A faint border or a pencil icon on hover or at rest would help the owner find the feature.

The Understand demo takes up about 600px of a 3440 screen, and 77–80% of the screen is empty (both sheet.png files). That is acceptable for a prose demo, but at 1920 the "Try your own" box sits below the fold, so a reader sees no hint that they can try it themselves.

The parent page still says "Eleven classes live here" (ux/page.js:110), and ux/readme.md's index lists eleven modules without Understand or Rename (docs-check.md flags the same thing). The new cards appear on the /framework/ux/ wall, but the text beside them is now out of date. The owner needs to decide who fixes it, because the brief fenced those files off.

The diff also includes the sibling minion's Servex/agents/hitl.js and route (diff.patch:1–220). That part looks sound: named ops only, `system` and `model` are refused, and the proof uses a fake `run_query`. This task did not need to touch it.

Both modules cover what the owner asked. Understand draws ✓/? after each sentence, and an unclear sentence gets a Decision card with two options and nothing pre-chosen; choosing one flips ? to ✓ and logs in memory. Rename selects a title on tap, then a button or typing "rename this" opens a dropdown of 5 names plus "keep current", and the log shows beneath. Both fall back to fixtures and say so in one line (Understand.js:685, Rename.js:285).

The review screenshots only cover 1280, 1920 and 3440 (Understand/sheet.png, Rename/sheet.png). None shows 400px, the dropdown open, or a clarification choice made. The brief made those required proof (requirements.md deliverable 4) because the owner tests on the phone, so check that the minion's own task-dir shots include them before landing.

On Rename/sheet.png the three titles look like plain h3 headings. Nothing says "card" or "tap me" until you hover or tap. A faint border or background on the unselected state (Rename.css:234) would make the first tap obvious, especially on a phone, where there is no hover.

Several Rename titles can be selected at once, because select() only toggles its own card (Rename.js:353). "First it kind of selects that card" reads as one selection at a time, so tapping one card could deselect the others through the shared demo.

The ? mark (Understand.js:775) and the Rename title (Rename.js:336) are role="button" with tabindex, but they only react to click. Enter and Space do nothing, so keyboard users can focus them and not press them.

The fixtures hedge rule treats "some" and "might" as hedges (Understand/fixtures.js:7). On "Try your own", most ordinary prose will get a ?, and every ? asks the same generic "literally or rough idea?" instead of "Did you mean A or B?". This is fine for the canned paragraph, but it is weak for the owner's own text while Servex is down.
Understand.js is 207 lines against a budget of about 150; Rename.js is 175. Each file also holds its own demo class, so moving the Demo into page.js would bring both back to size.
